intro: Here on the Mediterranean, in Mersin province, lies Anemurium. Its story runs from the 4th century BC to the 7th century AD. This well-preserved Roman and late Roman coastal city stands out for its baths, its aqueduct and its vast necropolis. Shall we explore?
history: Anemurium was founded beside Cape Anamur, and in the Roman and Byzantine periods it was an important port on the Eastern Mediterranean trade route. Then came the Arab raids of the 7th century, and the city was largely abandoned. Yet it was not entirely forgotten: in the 12th century, under the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, it was partly reoccupied.
structure-1: You are now at the Roman Baths. These baths had underfloor heating, with hot rooms and cold rooms. Imagine moving from one to the next, as bathers did here long ago.
structure-2: And here is the aqueduct. Its arches carried water from a distant source all the way to the city. Think of the effort it took to bring water to Anemurium.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Odeon, the vast Necropolis and the Byzantine Church.
facts: Did you know? Anemurium lies right beside Cape Anamur, the southernmost point of Asia Minor and of Anatolia, only 64 km from Cyprus; on a clear day, the coast of Cyprus is visible 64 kilometres away. With over three hundred monumental tombs, most of them two-storeyed and vaulted, it has one of the largest necropolises of the ancient world. And with two bath complexes, two theatres and mosaic-floored churches, the city lies just as it was left, sloping down to the sea.
outro: This brings our journey through Anemurium to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
